title: An inch is exactly 2.54cm
hook: Which conversion avoids the shown rounding shortcut?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that an inch is exactly 2.54 cm, and the error from using 2.5 grows with length, to more than 3 cm on a 2 m piece

misconception: Dividing by 2.5 to turn centimetres into inches is close enough for any length.
objective: The inch is defined as exactly 25.4 millimetres. Dividing centimetres by 2.54 gives inches; using 2.5 is a convenient approximation with a visible error that grows with length.

claims.text: The inch is defined as exactly 25.4 millimetres. Dividing centimetres by 2.54 gives inches; using 2.5 is a convenient approximation with a visible error that grows with length.
claims.source: NIST, SI Units - Length, https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/si-units-length (opened 2026-10-14), exact inch definition 25.4mm. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. NIST page not opened (web blocked). Opened instead: pint 0.26.1 (PyPI) default_en.txt, group USCSLengthInternational: 'inch = yard / 36' and 'yard = 0.9144 * meter ... # since Jul 1959', so 1 in = 0.0254 m = 25.4 mm exactly. Secondary source (a units registry), recorded so a reviewer can weigh it. Error grows with length: p/2.5 - p/2.54 = 0.0063 p in, proportional to p (stage conversion model).

recall.question: Convert 127 cm to inches using the exact definition of the inch.
recall.why: An inch is exactly 2.54 cm, so 127 ÷ 2.54 = 50 in. The 2.5 shortcut gives 50.8 in, and its error grows with length. The measurement itself still has its own uncertainty.
